what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat a bladder condition called interstitial cystitis, which causes bladder pain, pressure, and a frequent need to urinate. It is placed directly into the bladder to help reduce pain and inflammation.
how_to_take: This medicine is given by a healthcare provider in a clinic or doctor's office. A small, flexible tube (catheter) is inserted into your bladder, and the liquid medicine is slowly put directly into the bladder. You will be asked to hold the medicine in your bladder for about 15 minutes before letting it out. Your doctor will tell you how often you need to come in for treatments.
dosing: The usual treatment is one session every 1 to 2 weeks, for a total of 6 sessions. Your doctor may adjust this schedule based on how you respond to treatment. Do not try to use this medicine at home on your own — it must be given by a trained healthcare professional.
missed_dose: If you miss or need to reschedule a treatment appointment, call your doctor's office as soon as possible to set up a new time. Try not to skip treatments, as staying on schedule helps the medicine work best.
storage: This medicine is stored and handled by your healthcare provider. If for any reason you have it at home, keep it at room temperature, away from heat, light, and moisture. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze it.
what_to_avoid: You may notice a garlic-like or oyster-like odor on your breath and skin for up to 72 hours (3 days) after each treatment — this is normal and will go away on its own. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery right after treatment if you feel any discomfort or dizziness. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as DMSO can increase the effects of some medications.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe burning or pain in the bladder that does not go away, signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, blood in your urine, fever or chills, signs of a bladder infection such as increased burning with urination or foul-smelling urine, or vision changes. Go to the emergency room or call 911 if you have trouble breathing or severe swelling.
when_it_works: Some patients may notice improvement after the first few treatments, but it often takes the full course of 6 treatments to feel the best results. Some people may need repeat treatment cycles if symptoms come back. Talk with your doctor if you do not notice any improvement.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before receiving this treatment, as the safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. Older adults and patients with kidney or liver problems should be closely monitored by their doctor during treatment. This medicine is not approved for use in children.
